target_customer: African small and medium businesses needing invoicing, credit against receivables, payments and cash flow tools
problem: African SMBs faced a liquidity gap and slow payment collection; Swipe started with invoicing and then moved to credit and cash advances as Float.
business_model: fees and interest on credit, cash advances and B2B payments, plus accounting software
product_category: B2B payments, credit and accounting for SMBs

founders.name: Jesse Ghansah
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists the founder as Jesse Ahin; TechBuild and WeeTracker name him Jesse Ghansah.

founders.name: Barima Effah
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder of Swipe in TechBuild (Jan 2022) and WeeTracker (Sep 2023); not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Invoicing and payments software with credit underwriting and cross border treasury across several African markets, requiring banking partnerships and risk systems.

defensibility.rationale: Receivables credit and invoicing had few technical barriers and depended on capital and risk management rather than proprietary technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying it; the company's own problems, not incumbent action, dominated its later history.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in June 2021 framed a 300 billion dollar liquidity gap for African SMBs, and the company reported 10 million dollars of credit spending and cash advances in its first seven months live.

rebrands.why: Coverage ties the rename to the shift from invoicing to credit against receivables and the June 2021 product launch; the company's own stated reason was not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Float gained funding press in January 2022, but the brand's reputation was later damaged by 2023 reports about customer withdrawals; sources do not show the name driving growth.

pivots.from: Invoicing and invoice factoring as Swipe
pivots.to: Credit lines and cash advances for SMBs as Float
pivots.why: Per press, the company renamed itself to extend credit to businesses against their receivables.

outcome_analysis: Swipe pivoted to Float in mid 2021 and raised a 17 million dollar equity and debt seed in January 2022, then bought Accounteer. In 2023 WeeTracker and TechCabal reported unanswered client withdrawals, alleged misappropriation and FX trading losses, with an estimated 6 million dollars stuck for some startup clients. A later list of failed African startups includes Float, but no formal shutdown date or cause statement was found.
notes: The directory status is Active, but 2023 reporting describes serious distress and a later failed startups list includes Float; no shutdown announcement was found, so exit type is unknown. WeeTracker's allegations are allegations from clients, not findings; one low quality page conflated Float with Kippa and was ignored. The seed amount of 17 million dollars is split into 7 million equity and 10 million debt per TechBuild; CB Insights lists 17.15 million dollars total. Aggregators list about 2 million dollars from Y Combinator and Soma Capital in 2021 to 2022 under Swipe, unverified. Accounteer was acquired in August 2022 (TechCabal). The TechBuild piece named Waya Money, Swipe Nigeria and Brass only in a 2022 closing paragraph, too late to list as competitors at founding; no competitor source dated near the batch was found.
